subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw solve this direct `read` token waste now with a compact binary-document fallback, or defer it to broader document extraction/provider-native file handling?
rationale: Source inspection proves the direct fallback remains missing, but the issue proposes multiple behaviors and has an open conflicting candidate PR, so automation should not choose the permanent user-visible behavior alone.

options.title: Port Safe Fallback
options.body: Add a small shared `read` guard for known binary document formats that returns a compact actionable unsupported-document message without parsing file contents.

options.title: Defer To Document Work
options.body: Keep this tied to broader extraction or provider-native file handling and accept that direct `read` can still waste tokens until that work lands.

options.title: Guidance Only
options.body: Update tool description or prompting to discourage binary document reads without changing runtime behavior.

recommendation.title: Port Safe Fallback
recommendation.body: Add a small shared `read` guard for known binary document formats that returns a compact actionable unsupported-document message without parsing file contents.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is on the read-tool wrapper and session read implementation where the decision would land.
